  • Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling

  • Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets

Own payments performance

  • Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves

  • Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate

  • Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling

  • Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits

  • Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it

Own the economics

  • Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks

  • Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation

  • Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call

  • Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants

Own the money movement

  • Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down

  • Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile

  • Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies

💥 Example Projects

  • Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it

  • Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market

  • Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data

  • Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching

  • Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia

  • Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar.

  • 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar)

  • Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team.

  • Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action. You solve, you don't observe

  • Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it

  • Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke

data.title: Patient Support Coordinator
data.description:
If you are brilliant with people, love solving problems and genuinely care about giving patients a great experience, this could be the role for you.

We are looking for a Patient Support Coordinator to join our growing team at Montu. This is a busy, hands-on role at the heart of our patient journey, supporting people who may be completely new to medical cannabis and helping make their experience with us as simple, smooth and reassuring as possible.

You will be speaking to patients every day, answering questions, coordinating appointments, supporting our clinicians and working across the business to get things sorted. Some days will be incredibly busy, priorities will change and you will need to think on your feet, so we need someone who takes ownership, stays calm and genuinely enjoys helping people.

The most important thing is the person. We can teach you our systems and processes. What we cannot teach is empathy, energy and the instinct to go that extra mile when someone needs your help.

If you are organised, proactive, great with people and want to be part of a team that is changing the way patients access medical cannabis in the UK, I would love to hear from you.

What is the job?

As a Patient Support Coordinator, you’ll be a key part of the pharmacy team and play an important role in ensuring Montu patients and clinicians receive a seamless, high-quality service. You’ll be one of the main points of contact for patients, supporting them throughout their journey while also working closely with our clinical and operational teams.

This is an exciting opportunity to join Montu’s growing UK team and contribute to the development of our patient-facing operations. You’ll need to be organised, proactive and patient-focused, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, highly regulated healthcare environment.

The Patient Support Coordinator sits within the pharmacy team and requires a dynamic, patient-centric individual who is passionate about helping patients and clinicians get the best out of the service.

You’ll support the day-to-day running of the patient journey, working closely with clinicians, operations, governance, product and technology teams to ensure patients receive a smooth and professional experience.

What will you be doing?

  • Answer patient queries by telephone and email, providing clear, professional and empathetic support.

  • Schedule and coordinate patient appointments to optimise the patient experience.

  • Handle appointment payments accurately and efficiently.

  • Maintain patients’ electronic health records, ensuring information is accurate and up to date.

  • Support the clinical team by:

    • Collecting patient data relating to long-term conditions.

    • Ensuring patients meet the criteria for an initial assessment in line with Montu’s inclusion and exclusion criteria.

    • Booking patients for initial and follow-up appointments.

    • Preparing for and taking minutes during multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings.

  • Support operational and clinical recruitment and onboarding activities.

  • Collate patient and service feedback and liaise with the Head of Governance regarding complaints and compliments.

  • Report incidents and significant events and work with the Head of Governance to support appropriate follow-up.

  • Support clinicians with operational queries and day-to-day service requirements.

  • Liaise with the Product and Tech Support teams to resolve technical issues.

  • Work closely with your line manager and the wider team to identify opportunities for service improvement.

  • Attend work-related meetings as required.

  • Maintain all mandatory training and remain familiar with company policies and SOPs.

  • Work flexibly across shifts when required.

What you need:

  • At least 2 years’ work experience.

  • Previous experience working in a healthcare environment is advantageous but not essential.

  • Excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills.

  • Good understanding of working within a highly regulated environment and following policies and SOPs.

  • High level of IT proficiency and confidence using multiple systems.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work under pressure, manage competing priorities and remain calm in a fast-paced environment.

  • Patient-focused, professional and proactive approach.

What we offer:

  • Competitive salary.

  • 25 days holiday, rising to 37 days after one year, rising to 30 day after year 3 plus bank holidays.

  • 5% matched pension.

  • Private Health Care

  • Enhanced Maternity and Paternity

  • Cycle-to-work scheme.

  • Opportunities for learning, development and career progression.

  • A dynamic, collaborative and supportive working environment.

  • The opportunity to make a meaningful impact on patients’ experiences and contribute to the growth of a forward-thinking healthcare organisation.

About Montu

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM). We are committed to transforming lives by improving access to safe and effective treatments while delivering an exceptional standard of care.

As a growing organisation, we offer a dynamic and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers, work collaboratively across teams and make a meaningful impact on patients’ lives.

Compensation: £28K

data.title: Medical Secretary - 12 Month Fixed Term
data.description:
What is the job?

Great patient care doesn't just happen in the consultation room, it starts with a well-organised, supported and connected team behind the scenes.

We are looking for a Medical Secretary to join Montu UK on a 12-month fixed-term maternity cover contract. In this fast-paced role, you'll be the organisational backbone of our clinical team, helping to keep everything running smoothly so our clinicians can focus on what they do best — delivering exceptional care to patients.

From coordinating clinician schedules and managing clinical administration to supporting meetings and keeping important documentation up to date, you'll play a key role in making sure our day-to-day operations run seamlessly. You'll be juggling priorities, solving problems and keeping things moving, no two days are the same.

If you're highly organised, naturally proactive, enjoy supporting others and get satisfaction from making sure everything is exactly where it needs to be, you'll fit right in.

This is a full-time, fixed-term maternity cover contract for 12 months, working 40 hours per week.

What will you be doing?

As our Medical Secretary, you will be at the heart of keeping the clinical team organised and supported by:

  • Preparing, maintaining and updating clinician rotas to ensure excellent clinical coverage.

  • Resolving rota conflicts and communicating schedule changes quickly and effectively.

  • Providing day-to-day administrative support to clinicians and the wider medical team.

  • Maintaining accurate clinical records and ensuring documentation is always up to date.

  • Organising meetings, taking minutes and following up on agreed actions.

  • Coordinating consultant inductions and supporting onboarding and training activities.

  • Working closely with other departments to ensure clinicians have the equipment, systems and support they need to do their jobs effectively.

  • Acting as the first point of contact for clinician queries relating to scheduling and administration.

  • Drafting professional correspondence and supporting day-to-day communications.

  • Managing sensitive information with the highest level of confidentiality and professionalism.

  • Supporting operational projects and helping the team stay on track with key deadlines.

  • Identifying opportunities to improve processes and make the clinical team's day-to-day operations even more efficient.

What do you need?

We're looking for someone who loves being organised, takes pride in supporting others and thrives when there's plenty to keep them busy. You'll be comfortable managing multiple priorities, confident communicating with different people and able to stay calm and solution-focused in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

You'll ideally have:

  • Previous experience in a Medical Secretary, healthcare administration or similar administrative role.

  • Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise a varied and fast-moving workload.

  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

  • Good IT skills and confidence using Microsoft Office and healthcare or scheduling systems.

  • High attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records.

  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach and the confidence to work independently.

  • The ability to handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

  • A genuine desire to support a clinical team and contribute to a positive patient experience.

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + usual bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

About Us

Montu UK is a leading digital health company specialising in cannabis-based medicines (CBPM), dedicated to improving patient access to safe and effective treatments. Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

As a fast-growing organisation, we are building something exciting in healthcare. We offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers, take ownership and make a genuine difference.

At Montu UK, you are not simply supporting a clinical team, you are helping make better healthcare more accessible to patients. Your work has a direct impact on the smooth running of our services and the experience patients receive at every stage of their journey.

data.title: HR Partner (ER, Performance, Leadership)
data.description:
What is the job?
We’re scaling fast, doing things differently, and we’re looking for a HR Partner. Someone that thrives using creativity and deep ER & people expertise to guide people managers in an environment that has variety and the occasional bit of chaos that comes with startup life.

This is a hands-on, people-first role where you’ll partner closely with our rapidly growing Patient Experience function, supporting managers and teams through a period of significant growth and transformation. You’ll play a key role in shaping the employee experience, building management capability, and helping teams perform at their best in a fast-paced operational environment.

This role is not for a HR generalist. It is for a true subject matter expert, that specialises in employee relations, performance, coaching managers through complex situations and driving people initiatives. You’ll be right at the heart of the action and a trusted partner to the business, spending time at both our London (Kings Cross) and Winnersh (Reading) offices every week.

What will you be doing?

  • Partner closely with Team Leads and Managers across the Patient Experience team to provide day-to-day HR support and guidance on all matters employee relations, performance management & development and people coaching.

  • Act as a trusted advisor on people matters including performance management, wellbeing, absence, conduct and employee relations

  • Support the full employee lifecycle from induction and probation through to progression and offboarding

  • Coach and support managers to lead confidently, effectively and in line with company culture and values

  • Work closely with recruitment and onboarding teams to ensure a smooth and positive experience for all new starters

  • Support and lead on employee relations matters including investigations, performance concerns, welfare discussions and probation reviews

  • Collaborate with the Head of People & Talent on key people initiatives, process improvements and wider People projects

  • Help embed and improve key people processes such as engagement surveys, performance check-ins, recognition initiatives and manager development

  • Use data, trends and employee feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and proactively solve problems

  • Support policy implementation and provide practical HR guidance in line with UK employment law and best practice

  • Build strong relationships across operational teams and become a trusted and visible People partner within the business

  • Support change, growth and organisational development as the business continues to scale rapidly

What do you need?

  • Strong HRBP experience within a fast-paced, high-growth or operational environment where you have been supporting new & seasoned managers with complex people management, performance and development challenges.

  • Experience supporting large frontline or customer-focused teams is highly desirable

  • Comfortable working in ambiguity and adapting quickly as priorities evolve

  • Confidence handling employee relations matters with a calm, fair and pragmatic approach

  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills with the ability to influence and support managers at different levels

  • Highly organised with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing demands

  • A proactive, solutions-focused mindset with a willingness to roll up your sleeves and get stuck in

  • Self-sufficient and comfortable working remotely whilst collaborating closely with UK-based teams

  • Working knowledge of UK employment law is beneficial but not essential

  • Experience using HR systems such as HiBob is advantageous but not required

What we offer:

  • Generous Leave: 25 days holiday (rising to 27 after year one and 30 after year three) + usual bank holidays

  • Pension Matching: Up to 5% employer matching contributions

  • Flexibility and Wellness: Work-from-home options, cycle-to-work scheme, private healthcare and more

  • Growth Opportunities: Collaborate across teams and represent Montu at events, with support to grow your skills and impact

  • Enhanced Maternity & Paternity Leave

Our mission is to transform lives by combining innovative technology with high-quality clinical care, ensuring patients receive the support they need at every step of their journey.

As a fast-growing organisation, we offer a collaborative and supportive environment where talented people can develop their careers while contributing to meaningful change in healthcare. data.title: Senior Counsel, Commercial - EU / UK
data.description:
Marqeta is seeking a Senior Counsel, Commercial who will be an integral member of Marqeta’s Commercial Legal Team and strategic partner to the Revenue, Product and Finance Teams in the UK / EU Region.

As Senior Commercial Counsel, you will provide legal and business advice relating to commercial contracts entered into by Marqeta or Marqeta’s EU/UK subsidiaries, including agreements with customers, banks and network partners, and vendors in the EU and UK, and will help improve Marqeta’s contracting processes and procedures in the region. You will have a broad range of responsibilities and work in close partnership with cross-functional and geographically diverse teams supporting the development and delivery of Marqeta’s payment products and services. You will report to the Director, Assistant General Counsel.

This role will be based out of our London office in Holborn two days a week. Please speak to the recruiter for further details. We'd love for you to join us!

The Impact You’ll Have

  • Work with sales, partnership, and procurement teams to support the sale and development of Marqeta’s products and services with a focus on Marqeta’s customers and partners in Europe. Specifically, you will negotiate strategic, complex and cross-border agreements with Marqeta’s customers and partners within Europe.

  • Assist with resolving complex issues in strategic customer, bank and network partner, and vendor agreements in Europe.

  • Support Marqeta’s expansion by partnering with cross-functional teams in sales, product, compliance, bank partnerships, and finance to help sell Marqeta’s products and services in Europe.

  • Work collaboratively across the Legal, Regulatory and Compliance team on cross-functional priorities and initiatives.

  • Collaborate on the development of agreement templates and playbooks for the Commercial Legal Team to drive scale, and cross-functional efficiencies, and offer creative solutions where appropriate.

  • Provide practical legal advice to the business and develop strong working relationships across the Company with cross-functional peers and other business stakeholders.

Who You Are

  • 4-7 years of experience practicing either in-house or at a reputable law firm, with at least 2 years working in or advising companies in the payments, fintech or financial services space

  • An eagerness to learn, a can-do attitude, and an interest (and ideally some experience working) in the payments industry

  • A solutions-oriented attorney who doesn’t rabbit-hole on theoretical risk but instead focuses on practical risk-based solutions to legal issues

  • Experience drafting and negotiating contracts for payments companies, fintech companies or financial institutions

  • An understanding of laws and regulations pertaining to financial services and technology (including Payment Services Directives; Anti-Money Laundering Directives; GDPR; Interchange Fee Regulations and EBA Guidelines)

  • A keen sense of ownership, and adaptability to a fast-changing environment

  • Sound judgment and ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively

  • Willingness and ability to support colleagues and initiatives across multiple time zones

Recruiter for this role

  • Lou Devlin - Linkedin Profile (no agencies please!)

Typical Process

  • Application Submission

  • Recruiter video call

  • Hiring manager video call

  • Virtual “Onsite” consisting of 4, 45 min calls

  • Offer!

Compensation and Benefits

  • Premium Private Medical and Dental coverage

  • Generous time off program with additional “Floating Holiday days”

  • Retirement savings program with company contribution

  • Equity in a publicly-traded company and an Employee Stock Purchase Program

  • Monthly stipend to support our remote work model

  • Annual development stipend to support our people's growth and development

  • Family-forming benefits and up to 20 weeks of Parental Leave

  • Wellbeing programs i.e. Modern Health, HealthKick and much more…

About Marqeta

Marqeta is on a mission to change the way money moves. We’re one of the earliest enablers of embedded finance, a market opportunity sized up in the trillions. Our card issuing platform provides unprecedented flexibility and control for companies to issue cards, authorize transactions, and manage payment operations in real time. Marqeta is powering the most well known brands in the new economy (Block, Cash App, Affirm, Instacart, Doordash, Uber, Walmart, etc). You don’t need to be a Payments expert to join the Marqeta Team, let us help you with that. This is the opportunity of a lifetime to work with innovators around the world and unlock equitable financial access for all.

Marqeta’s Values

– Solve for the Customer: With a deep understanding of our customers' business and empathy for their needs, we deliver products and services that drive their success. Earning and keeping their trust guides everything we do.

– Do What's Right: Knowing businesses and livelihoods depend on us, we pursue solutions that disrupt responsibly and deliver high-quality results that our customers count on. We own our work from start to finish.

– Simplify and Innovate: We approach challenges with curiosity and take smart risks. Innovation comes from finding better, simpler ways to achieve extraordinary outcomes.

– Win as a Team: We succeed together by embracing diverse perspectives and pushing each other to raise the bar. We lead with humility and set aside hierarchy to work as a team.

– Make it Count: We drive forward with focus and agility. With a sense of urgency and purpose, we get the job done, and done right.

Equal Employment Opportunity, Accommodations and Privacy

Marqeta is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, childbirth, or related medical conditions), veteran status or uniformed service member status, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship or immigration status, physical or mental disability, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, genetic information (including testing or characteristics) or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Marqeta endeavors to make reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to submit this application, complete any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participate in the employee selection process, please submit this form with your specific accommodation request.

Marqeta cares about your privacy. Personal data that is provided as part of the application and recruitment process is processed in accordance with the Applicant Privacy Notice. Additional information for California residents can be found here.

data.title: HR Advisor
data.description:
HR Advisor


Office Location: Basingstoke, United Kingdom

Working Arrangement: Hybrid Working

Join Our Team as an HR Advisor!

Are you passionate about guiding managers, resolving employee relations cases, and creating workplace experiences that bring out the best in people?

We are looking for a dedicated HR Advisor to join our team in Basingstoke. As a frontline people partner, you will play a critical role in delivering seamless HR operations, championing company culture, and ensuring our people strategy aligns with our overall business goals.

If you are a skilled HR generalist with a strong foundation in employee relations, a solid grasp of UK employment law, and a passion for supporting people at every stage of their career journey, this is the perfect next step for your HR career.

What Your Day Will Look Like

As an HR Advisor, you will act as a trusted advisor to management and employees across the organisation, providing clear advice on a wide range of HR topics while reporting directly to the Senior HR Business Partner.

One day you might be coaching a manager through a performance improvement plan, handling an employee relations case (disciplinary, grievance, or absence management), or updating HR policies to keep pace with changing employment legislation. The next, you could be drafting offer letters and onboarding new hires, analysing turnover trends in Workday, or coordinating interactive learning workshops and employee engagement activities.

You will balance day-to-day HR operations with strategic people projects, working closely with recruitment, department managers, and leadership to drive performance and cultivate an inclusive workplace culture.

What We Value

We move fast, collaborate closely, and support one another in delivering exceptional people experiences.

You'll fit right in if you:

  • Drive sound HR advice grounded in a practical understanding of employment law and best practices

  • Possess strong conflict-resolution skills, approaching complex people issues with critical thinking and empathy

  • Communicate exceptional balance, maintaining total confidentiality while navigating sensitive situations

  • Organise with agility, effortlessly juggling multiple active ER cases and HR initiatives simultaneously

  • Thrive on data and tech, using platforms like Workday to spot trends and deliver meaningful HR insights

  • Build strong relationships, acting as an approachable, supportive partner to employees and managers alike

Your Background

You don't need to tick every box, but we're generally looking for:

Core Skills & Expertise

  • HR Experience: 2–4 years of generalist HR experience, with hands-on practice managing end-to-end ER casework (disciplinaries, grievances, PIPs, and absence management)

  • Education & Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)

  • Employment Law: Strong working knowledge of local labor regulations, policy maintenance, and workplace compliance

  • Tech Proficiency: Hands-on experience with Workday or similar HRIS platforms, alongside MS Office / Google Workspace

Competent / Working Knowledge

  • Supporting annual performance management, bonus cycles, and manager coaching

  • Talent acquisition support, including interviewing, offer creation, and onboarding execution

  • Identifying training needs and coordinating L&D programs or workshops

  • Employee engagement initiatives, survey data analysis, and workplace wellbeing planning

And we make sure it’s a great place to work:

  • 25 days of paid leave per year

  • Pension program

  • Discounts for staff

  • Office games like FIFA, chess, and ping-pong

  • Sony Benefits and much more!

Why Level Up Your Career With Us

  • Trusted Impact: Become a go-to strategic advisor for managers and employees across the business

  • Skill Growth: Expand your ER, compliance, and L&D expertise alongside an experienced Senior HR Business Partner

  • Culture Driver: Take lead ownership of engagement surveys, team-building events, and wellbeing initiatives

  • Operational Excellence: Utilize modern HR systems like Workday to streamline reporting and drive business decisions

data.title: Engineering Leader
data.description:
About Ema

Ema is building the world’s leading Agentic AI platform to transform enterprise productivity. We enable organizations to delegate repetitive tasks to Ema, the Universal AI Employee, delivering 10x gains in workforce efficiency, across functions. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production — we ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Leader to manage and scale multiple product lines in the Voice, BPO, and Workforce Management space. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of real-time voice systems, operations research, and data-intensive platform engineering.

You will report directly to the Head of Engineering and own the engineering organization that builds the infrastructure powering Ema’s Voice AI Employees, Agent QA, auto-learning pipelines, rich analytics, and workforce optimization capabilities — all operating as scalable, multi-tenant systems deployed across global geographies.

You will collaborate with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to translate customer needs into production systems that handle high volumes of voice data, deliver real-time insights, and continuously improve through automated learning loops. As the owner of multiple product lines, you will balance roadmap priorities across Voice, BPO operations, and WFM (work force management) — ensuring each product evolves cohesively while meeting distinct customer needs.

What You Will Do

Scalable Multi-Tenant Systems

  • Architect and build multi-tenant systems that serve enterprise customers across geographies with strict data residency, isolation, and compliance requirements.

  • Design high-throughput ingestion systems capable of processing large volumes of voice data, call metadata, and operational telemetry in near real-time.

  • Make foundational architectural decisions on data stores, stream processing, and storage tiers — balancing query performance, cost, and operational simplicity.

  • Champion SOLID principles, clean architecture, and engineering rigor across all codebases — ensuring systems are testable, extensible, and maintainable at scale.

Team Building & Engineering Culture

  • Recruit, hire, and develop senior engineers across a multi-disciplinary function spanning voice engineering, backend systems, data engineering, and applied operations research.

  • Establish engineering standards, code review culture, and a strong bias toward shipping — with equal commitment to system reliability and customer experience.

  • Coach and grow senior/staff engineers into technical leaders; manage engineering managers as the organization scales.

  • Drive cross-functional alignment with Product, ML/AI, and Go-to-Market teams to ensure the platform evolves in lockstep with customer needs and market feedback.

Voice Platform & Agent QA

  • Own the end-to-end engineering for Ema’s AgentQA capabilities — real-time voice pipelines, telephony integrations, and voice-to-action workflows.

  • Build and scale the Agent QA platform: automated call scoring, compliance monitoring, sentiment analysis, and coaching feedback loops.

  • Design auto-learning systems that continuously improve voice agents from production interactions — closed-loop feedback, model retraining triggers, and quality regression detection.

  • Deliver rich voice analytics: call volume trends, handle time distributions, first-call resolution metrics, agent performance dashboards, and anomaly detection.

  • Build scalable voice pipeline across geographies – keeping in mind PII, security and compliance requirements.

Workforce Management & Operations Research

  • Build WFM capabilities including demand forecasting, shift scheduling, real-time adherence monitoring, and capacity planning — applying operations research techniques to optimize workforce utilization.

  • Design and implement optimization algorithms for headcount modeling, skill-based routing, and workload balancing across multi-site, multi-timezone contact center operations.

  • Partner with ML/AI teams to integrate predictive models for call volume forecasting, attrition risk, and staffing efficiency.

What We Look For

Required

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years leading engineering teams of 8+ engineers at high-growth startups or top-tier tech companies.

  • Deep expertise in building real-time, data-intensive systems.

  • Strong foundation in data stores and storage systems: relational databases, time-series stores, columnar analytics engines, and caching layers — with the judgment to choose the right tool for the workload.

  • Experience building quality software using AI-driven tools and workflows.

  • Track record of taking products from 0→1 and iterating rapidly based on customer feedback.

  • Hands-on proficiency with SOLID principles, clean architecture, and design patterns — you write and review production code and lead by example on system design.

  • Experience building scalable multi-tenant SaaS platforms with data isolation, geo-distributed deployments, and compliance requirements (SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA).

  • Track record of building ingestion systems for high volumes of load — event-driven architectures, stream processing (Kafka, Flink, or equivalent), and batch/real-time hybrid pipelines.

  • Strong product sense: ability to deeply understand customer problems in contact center, voice, and workforce domains and translate them into clean technical solutions.

  • Proven ability to hire, develop, and retain high-caliber engineers across multiple disciplines in competitive markets.

Good to have

  • Experience in voice/telephony systems: WebRTC, SIP, voice-over-IP infrastructure, or contact center platforms.

  • Background in operations research or optimization: scheduling algorithms, linear/integer programming, constraint satisfaction, or demand forecasting models.

  • Experience building analytics platforms: OLAP systems, real-time dashboards, metric computation engines, or BI infrastructure.

  • Prior work on auto-learning or continuous improvement systems: feedback loops from production data, automated retraining pipelines, or quality monitoring systems.

  • Experience with AI/ML-powered products in enterprise settings — agentic automation, LLM orchestration, or AI-driven UX.

  • Familiarity with WFM or contact center operations — staffing models, Erlang-based capacity planning, or real-time adherence systems.

Why Ema

  • Build at the intersection of Voice AI, operations research, and enterprise-scale systems — a rare combination of deeply technical challenges with direct customer impact.

  • Shape the engineering foundation of a category-defining AI platform — your architectural decisions will power how the world’s largest enterprises run their voice and workforce operations.

  • High-impact, high-visibility role with direct access to the Head of Engineering, co-founders, and enterprise customers.

  • A team of exceptional engineers from Google, Meta, Microsoft Research, and top CS programs worldwide.

  • Competitive compensation, meaningful equity, and the opportunity to build something that matters.

data.description:
A platform you can believe in: Immersive One is the leading cyber resilience solution across the globe.

Build and scale a best in class platform alongside a team of the brightest minds in cybersecurity! At Immersive, we’re uniquely positioned to future-proof organizations against any cyber challenge. If that excites you, read on!


Immersive helps prove and improve your cyber resilience, by simulating real-world threats, testing your skills, and measuring performance. We put your readiness to the ultimate test. From sharpening technical capabilities to making high-pressure decisions, our platform allows you to assess every angle, pinpoint areas for growth, and prove your ability to tackle evolving threats with unwavering confidence.

https://www.immersivelabs.com/why-immersive-labs


Immersive was founded in 2017, from a cargo container in Bristol, UK we’ve grown to over 300 employees globally, announced funding of more than £150 million and been voted a Best place to work on multiple occasions!

https://www.immersivelabs.com/company/our-story

Senior Cyber Security Engineer - Red Team

Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next Senior Cyber Security Engineer?

Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced cyber professional within the offensive security sector - with expertise in conducting red team engagements - to join our Product team as Senior Cyber Security Engineer - Red Team.

If successful you will join our Cyber team working closely with our Cyber Team Leads as we embark on this exciting new phase of product development within our market leading cyber resilience platform.

This isn’t an ordinary red team role - we know everyone claims this and will tell you their role is super unique…but this one really is.

You are constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things offensive security related, from red teaming, to the latest AI driven attacks, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges.

You will be a key player in our Red Team Content team, shaping and influencing the roll out of our offensive security and AI pen test content roadmap, simulating attack paths and helping train our users to counter the latest threats.

You will be educating the world of offensive security professionals on how to make sure they are secure in what they do. Now that is a pretty cool legacy to leave behind.

Your mission (if you choose to accept it) is to evolve and disrupt within the Red Team space by creating emulated environments within our platform that will simulate both hacking and defending in an engaging and intuitive way for our community.

You will design, build and deliver practical and theory content to gamify offensive security and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way.

If you have a passion for cyber security, are experienced in the area of offensive security, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market leading platform, Immersive One.

Your main responsibilities (we're scaling fast, so these may change as we grow):

  • Utilising knowledge of pen test and red teaming engagements and techniques to plan, write and improve offensive security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform.

  • Produce multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification

  • Test Red Team labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected

  • Research vulnerabilities, tools and offensive tactics and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users

  • Compile technical research into understandable concise content for both technical and non-technical audience

  • Work with the wider Product team on new projects and product innovations and how best to deploy them

Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas:

  • A number of years of experience working in offensive security as a penetration tester or as a Offensive Security Consultant

  • In-depth knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework and how it is used to help enterprises deal with threats to their organisation.

  • Have a strong technical understanding of networking, computing and cyber security concepts

  • Have the ability to use examples and analogies to simplify complex subjects - your content will train real world users to identify and combat the latest threats so you need to be able to inhabit the mindset of your target audience to create realistic simulations

  • Familiarity with Linux, Docker and Python would be beneficial

  • Attitude and approach is just as important as technical skills for this role - you will be someone who enjoys tackling complex problems and finding the solution. You'll be a natural problem solver and 'tinkerer' who enjoys prototyping and iteration.

Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role:

  • Driven - We push the boundaries of innovation, acting swiftly to achieve ambitious outcomes. Our drive embodies a culture of ambition, where challenges are stepping stones to excellence.

  • Inclusive - Our strength lies in diversity, fostering a culture where every individual contributes to our collective strength. We champion open dialogue and empathy, ensuring a collaborative, inclusive workplace.

  • Customer Centric - We seek to develop deep relationships with our customers to help them achieve their business outcomes. We exceed our customers and partners' expectations by crafting products, services and experiences that surprise, delight and ensure they feel valued and supported every day.

  • One Team - We are a talented global team working together to achieve our vision. Central to our ethos, resilience means adapting and thriving in adversity. It guides our innovation, ensuring we and our clients are prepared for the future.

We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work. Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application!


As well as an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you. We offer an extensive range of benefits so you can do your very best work:

  • Time off, flexible and remote working so you can work when is best for you, includes 25 days annual leave + 2 volunteering days and your birthday off

  • The longer you are with Immersive, the more holiday days you get, up to a maximum of 30 days after five years of service

  • Look after your family and yourself with enhanced parental leave, mindfulness groups, critical illness cover, 7% matched pension, private healthcare plan and more

  • Career and learning development through the platform, a dedicated professional development fund and our ‘Learn Anything’ fund - which enables you to learn anything that’s not work!

  • Recognition & Rewards for doing great work and living our values and behaviours

  • Informal or formal flexible working options, e.g. flexible start and finish times, reduced hours

  • We have a vibrant team culture with team events throughout the year. Our socials have included everything from pottery painting and paper mask making, to dungeons and dragons!

  • When you do visit the UK hub, getting there is easy: we’re based in the centre of Bristol, just a 10 minute walk from the train station. We also offer railcard loan and cycle scheme to buy a new bike

Find out more about life at Immersive Labs https://careers.immersivelabs.com


Cyber threats wait for no one and neither should you. Apply now!

What is Jedox?

Jedox is a global leader in Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) and a recognized Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader, helping organizations transform fragmented planning into connected, data-driven decision-making.

At the heart of the platform is JedoxAI - a multi-agent intelligence engine delivering explainable, AI-powered forecasting, natural-language insights and AIssisted™ planning - putting Jedox at the forefront of the shift to AI-driven performance management.


Your Responsibilities

As a Sales Account Executive (m/f/d) within the Jedox team, you will play a key part in helping enterprise customers to transform their planning, forecasting and performance management processes. Acting as a trusted advisor, you will use a value-based sales approach to show how Jedox provides modern, digital and integrated enterprise performance and analysis (xP&A) solutions.

In this role, you will own the entire sales process for enterprise customers, from identifying potential clients to closing deals. You will promote Jedox as the ideal solution for xP&A initiatives, work closely with internal teams and develop long-term relationships with customers and partners, while maintaining a strong focus on value, trust and sustainable success.

We are building a high-performing team defined by ownership, accountability and energy. This is a genuinely exciting time to join: AI is reshaping how every finance team plans and forecasts, and Jedox is right at the centre of that conversation - giving you a fresh, differentiated story to take to market. If you're a motivated seller who enjoys being out in front of customers and partners, and want to make your mark in an exciting company, you'll find real support, momentum and opportunity here.   • Build lasting relationships: Build trusted partnerships with customers, partners and internal stakeholders to ensure long-term success.


Your Profile

  • Over three years' experience in professional sales, ideally within the FP&A function.
  • Experience in Enterprise Performance Management or in selling analytics, AI, data, or ERP solutions.
  • Strong record of success in achieving and exceeding sales goals.
  • Proven ability to build, manage and self-generate a healthy sales pipeline and expand existing accounts.
  • A high-ownership mindset: you act with urgency, take responsibility for your results, and when challenges arise you come with ideas on how to tackle them together.

data.description:
💰 £25k-£60k, depending on experience and location

📍 UK / Europe / Remote

Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. We're an AI-powered, creator-first platform helping creators connect, engage, and earn directly from their audiences at scale. Fanvue has surpassed $200m+ in annual recurring revenue, with triple-digit year-on-year growth, supporting hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans worldwide.

As crypto usage on Fanvue's payment rails keeps growing, so does our exposure to crypto-specific fraud and financial crime. Recent cases have shown gaps in the Fraud team's crypto knowledge, and right now nobody on the team has dedicated crypto fraud or financial crime expertise. This role exists to build that capability from the ground up.

🎯 The Role

We're hiring Fanvue's first Fraud Investigator with dedicated crypto expertise, reporting to Head of Fraud. AI has taken our fraud detection as far as it can on crypto rails, what's missing is in-house subject matter expertise: someone who has used these investigation tools before, can set the strategy, and can train the rest of the team.

🚀 What You'll Do

  • Lead on investigating cases of potential fraud or financial crime where crypto rails are involved, including payment fraud, account takeover, and money laundering typologies on crypto on/off-ramps

  • Build out crypto-specific fraud investigation capability within the Fraud team: on-chain tracing methods, tooling, and documented process for crypto-related cases

  • Train the wider Fraud team on crypto fraud red flags and typologies, so risk indicators get caught earlier in standard triage, not just by you

  • Design how Fanvue prevents and detects crypto-related fraud and financial crime as the function matures

  • Work directly with vendors to get the most out of crypto investigation tooling and data

  • Support fraud and financial crime investigations where crypto isn't involved, as part of the wider Fraud team's caseload

  • Lead on escalations to law enforcement where relevant

  • Feed your expertise into loss prevention strategy across Fraud, product, and payments

👀 Who You Are

  • 3+ years investigating fraud and/or financial crime with specific crypto/blockchain exposure, from an exchange, blockchain analytics firm, bank crypto desk, or law enforcement crypto unit

  • A process creator and improver: you've played a role in designing or improving investigation techniques, not just following them

  • Comfortable being the subject matter expert. As our first crypto-focused Fraud hire, you'll build the wider team's knowledge while acting as the go-to for other parts of the business (payments, payouts, product) wherever crypto risk shows up

  • Familiar with crypto investigation tooling (e.g. Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic, etc.) and know how to get the most from it in a fraud prevention context

  • High ownership: excited by a large, expanding remit, and not afraid to break new ground without an existing playbook

✨ You'll Thrive Here If

  • You want to build a function from scratch rather than inherit one

  • You're energised by being the go-to expert and enjoy teaching others what you know

  • You like combining hands-on casework with process and systems design

data.title: Customer Success Manager
data.description:
Customer Success Manager

🌍 About us

Plinth is a fast-growing tech startup working with charities, foundations and local government. Small and local charities are highly effective but largely hidden. They have no spare time and no spare money. We're building the tools these organisations need and shining a light on the work they do. Read more on our blog.

🚀We're growing fast. 3-4x this year. We get 7+ new clients a month and we're shipping new features every few days. This means things move quickly and your work directly shapes how we scale. You'll have real responsibility from day one.

❤️It's really impactful work. Our clients are charities and grassroots organisations across the UK, and soon internationally. When you help them succeed with our platform, you're directly amplifying their impact. Every successful onboarding means a charity spends less time fighting with their systems and more time on their actual mission.

🤝You'll work with impressive people. Our team is talented, collaborative and slightly strange(?). We value impact, speed and openness. We work in person in our office in Old Street because we genuinely enjoy each other's company (most of the time). It’s a high trust, creative space where if you think something's a good idea, you just go do it.

💼 You need to be able to:

  • Work both fast and slow: You'll navigate slow public sector procurement cycles one minute, then help us ship a new feature over lunch the next. The whiplash is intense but it keeps things interesting.

  • Keep it real: You'll be getting the train to community centres and youth clubs where the heating doesn't work and where the paint is peeling off the walls. It’s rarely glamourous. You need to be willing to meet clients where they are, literally and figuratively.

  • Listen to problems, ignore solutions: Clients will tell you exactly what they think they need. Your job is to understand the actual problem and guide them to what will really work, even when they're convinced they already know the answer. This requires self-confidence, understanding of the platform and genuine listening in equal measure.

  • Teach people: Most of our clients don't love shiny gadgets. If you're the kind of person who enjoys teaching your gran to use a smartphone, this is ideal. You need to explain some fairly complex systems clearly without being condescending and still getting user adoption

  • Automate and document yourself away:🤖 We're small and growing fast. Build systems and processes that make your job increasingly redundant. There’s always plenty more to do.

  • Understand the difference between "urgent" and 🚨 URGENT — When you're managing 4-8 concurrent client projects and everyone thinks their issue is critical, you need to distinguish between what must happen for launch versus what can wait. This is harder than it sounds.

  • Grow with the role: we need someone who is comfortable with our clients and team doubling every 6 months. Your role will rapidly change to reflect that, but it leaves you with lots of room to grow in responsibility.

🧩 What kind of background do we think would be a good fit?

We’d expect a few years experience in something like the following:

  • Coaching / Tutoring: You know how to meet people where they are and guide them to better outcomes

  • Hospitality management: Service mindset, de-escalation skills, managing expectations when things don't go to plan, letting the customer think they’re right when they aren’t

  • Event/production management: Used to juggling moving pieces, keeping stakeholders calm, making last-minute pivots when things go wrong

  • Community organising/activism: Already comfortable in the spaces you'll be visiting, get the mission, used to working with limited resources

  • Consulting: You're used to parachuting into chaos, extracting actionable tasks, and keeping multiple clients calm simultaneously

  • User research/UX: Good at understanding what people actually need versus what they say they need, synthesising feedback into actionable insights

  • Knowledge of the charity sector is a significant advantage, whether that’s as an employee, consultant or as a long term volunteer.

  • It would also definitely be helpful if you have any technical experience to help with managing data migrations.

Importantly, This is a list of suggestions.

If you have experience in only some of this, or have only some of these skills, please do apply anyway.

📈 How can you measure your success?

  • Speed of getting customers successfully using Plinth: From signed contract to actively using the platform and seeing value.

  • Positive recommendations: Clients recommending us positively to their networks — it’s a big source of our growth.

  • Increasing use of Plinth: Clients expanding how they use the platform over time, not just maintaining baseline usage

🧠 The role

Client Onboarding (70%) — Lead onboarding from kick-off to go-live. Break down complex projects into clear phases. Manage timelines, priorities, and expectations across 7+ new clients per month. Stay on top of new features we ship every few days. Push back when needed and teach anyone regardless of background.

Operations & Process Improvement (30%) — Audit and optimise our support systems (expect to manage Intercom chat a couple of days a week). Refine onboarding workflows. Keep documentation current. Work with engineering to communicate what's urgent versus what's just a problem. Track feature requests across clients and synthesise them into product improvements.

💵 What we offer

  • Salary: £42,000 - £75,000 depending on experience

  • Equity as part of your package

  • Location: In-person, Old Street, London

☎️ Interview process

  1. Quick (20-30 min) call with Chris as a sanity check

  2. First interview with Chris and a co-founder

  3. Long (2-3 hour), quite intense, in-person interview — meet the team, do tasks, respond to case studies, be challenged

  4. Decision

data.title: Operations Associate
data.description:
TLDR: Plinth builds software for charities, foundations and funders. 2,000+ UK organisations use us, we add 7+ clients a month, and we ship constantly. HR, security, legal and finance currently sit with one person. That stops working at our next size. We're hiring someone to own a chunk of it: recruitment operations, contracts and invoicing, and the paperwork behind our ISO 27001 certification. You don't need to have done security or legal work before. You need to be the kind of person who picks up something unfamiliar, works out how it should run, then runs it properly.

What you'll own

  • Recruitment operations. The pipeline end to end. Keeping our tools current, booking interviews, wrangling schedules, first-pass CV screening, and working with team leads to build the tasks candidates get set. Candidates never wait on us

  • Contracting and invoicing. Contracts out, chased, signed and filed. Invoices raised and paid. Unglamorous, and it matters that someone holds it

  • Security administration. We're going through ISO 27001 now, and keeping a certification is more work than getting one. Reviews on a schedule, evidence that has to exist, paperwork that has to be generated. You own that calendar and it doesn't slip

  • Security questionnaires. Customers send long ones and they hold up deals. You'll answer them with support from the team and our internal tooling, and build a reusable answer bank so the tenth takes an hour instead of a day. You don't need to be a security expert. You do need to be confident enough to learn out loud

  • Automating the repeatable bits. A lot of this job is the same task on a loop, and a lot of it shouldn't be. Doing something by hand for the tenth time is a bug you're responsible for. You'll build the templates, automations and AI workflows that take it off your plate, then move on to harder work

  • Making the role bigger. Ops is four functions and one and a half people. As we grow, you're first in line for whatever you've shown you can hold

What we're looking for

  • You're the organiser. The one who books the group holiday, runs the spreadsheet and gets everyone to actually pay. That instinct is most of this job

  • You'll have a go at unfamiliar work. We'll hand you a contract, a security review, or a process nobody has written down. You won't be on your own with it, but we need someone whose instinct is to attempt it, ask a colleague to check it, and be better at it next time, rather than wait to be shown

  • You've probably done this shape of job. EA, team assistant, ops coordinator, office manager, practice manager. Somewhere you were the reliable centre of a lot of moving parts

  • Nothing gets quietly dropped. Interviews, invoices, an ISO review and a half-finished questionnaire, all live at once, none of them missing

  • You write clearly and fast. To candidates, to customers' IT teams, to a lawyer. Warm, plain, no waffle

  • Discretion. You'll be close to salary data, contracts and personal information from day one

  • You use AI properly. You've used Claude or similar beyond chatting: drafting, summarising, first passes at questionnaires, small workflows you built yourself. If you've touched Claude Code or automation tools, say so. It's how a small ops team keeps up with a company doubling every six months

Nice to have

  • Exposure to ISO 27001, SOC 2 or Cyber Essentials, from any angle

  • Experience with recruitment

  • Experience with contracts, procurement or finance admin

  • Charity, funder or local government background

What good looks like after a year

  • Recruitment runs without the Chief of Staff touching the logistics

  • ISO reviews and evidence are on schedule and audit-ready, with no scramble the week before

  • Security questionnaires come back in days, from a library you built, and stop blocking deals

  • The tasks you did by hand in month one are automated, templated, or gone

  • You own things outright that nobody else needs to think about

Logistics

  • Location: London, Old Street (4 days a week in office)

  • Hours: Full time

  • Salary: c.£50,000 depending on experience

  • Reports to: Chief of Staff, who leads operations

data.title: Customer Support Analyst
data.description:
TLDR: Plinth builds software for charities, foundations and funders. 13,000+ UK organisations use us, we add 7+ clients a month, and we ship constantly. We're hiring someone to own support as a system rather than work a queue. You'll be the first person customers reach, but you'll be judged on whether fewer of them need to reach you next quarter, and on being able to prove it. You'll also own free Plinth, which exists because it's good for the sector and because it's where we learn fastest. A strong first or second job: you'll touch support, product, engineering and operations in your first month.

What you'll own

  • Your own workload. You start as first responder in Intercom, and your job is to make that role smaller every quarter. Falling volume with rising satisfaction is the metric, not tickets closed

  • Measurement. PostHog, Intercom and Linear are yours: the ticket tagging that makes volume analysable, the dashboards showing where users get stuck, the view of whether fixes shipped and queries stopped. Right now we can't see our own support data clearly enough to know if we're improving. That's your problem to solve

  • Free Plinth. Thousands of small charities who could never afford software like this get it anyway, and they test new functionality at volume. You own their experience and argue their case internally, and know when it will make the product better for everyone.

  • Self-serve. Help articles, in-app guidance, website content and the chatbot behind them. A product with an audience, not a wiki that gets tidied when things are quiet

  • Support tooling. Find the queries that shouldn't need a human, then build or spec the thing that removes them: a status page, a clearer error message, an automation, a self-serve action. You're expected to spot it, make the case and see it land

  • The loop into product. Recommendations backed by evidence, not anecdote: here's the query volume, here's the funnel showing where it starts, here's what we change, here's how we'll know it worked. Then follow it until the cause is fixed, not the symptom

  • Escalation and response. Customers hear back in minutes, not tomorrow, and stay informed until it's genuinely resolved

What we're looking for

  • You work without handholding. We'll give you context and a clear idea of what good looks like, not a daily list

  • Repetition bothers you. Answering the same question by hand for the tenth time should feel like a bug you own

  • You think past the ticket in front of you: why did this reach me at all, and what would stop the next fifty

  • You reach for a number rather than a feeling. You don't need to arrive knowing PostHog, just to enjoy turning a messy pile of tickets into a chart that settles an argument

  • You'll advocate for users internally, including the ones who don't pay us

  • You're properly organised. Tickets, escalations, half-written articles and an invoice query all live at once, nothing quietly dropped

  • You write clearly and fast, to stressed non-technical people. Warm, unpatronising, honest when something's broken

  • You've run something yourself: a society, a side project, a process you rebuilt in a part-time job

  • Charity sector experience and technical confidence are both real advantages

What good looks like after a year

  • The top recurring queries from your first month no longer exist

  • Support volume per customer has fallen while the company has grown, and we can see it on a dashboard you built

  • Anyone at Plinth can answer "are we getting better at support?" in thirty seconds

  • You can point at paid features that shipped better because free users hit the problems first

Recent graduates welcome. We care more about how you think, write and organise yourself than what you've done before. If you want ownership rather than a narrow lane, this offers more range in a year than most graduate schemes manage in three.

Logistics

  • Location: London, Old Street (4 days a week in office)

  • Hours: Full time

  • Salary: 40-50k depending on experience

data.title: Ecommerce Brand Manager
data.description:
Entropy sells survival, power and preparedness gear in the US. Around $525k a year, currently at contribution margin neutral. Almost all of it is other people's product resold at 9-12% margin, which caps what the business can earn.

Own-brand product and better acquisition economics are the fix. That's the job.

You'd own the P&L and report to Jack and Lasse weekly. Nobody else is doing this.

Tasks

  • Own blended gross margin, moving it from 12% to 25%, and take the business through breakeven.
  • Source and launch own-brand SKUs. Suppliers, MOQ negotiation, samples, freight, duty, 3PL, listings, launch.
  • Run paid acquisition yourself. Google Shopping, PMax and Search. There's no agency and there won't be one.
  • Site and conversion work. Product pages, imagery, copy, checkout, cart abandonment.
  • Build attach and post-purchase revenue. Checkout upsells, replenishment, email flows.
  • Restart the content engine. Video cadence, TikTok, YouTube, UGC and reviews.
  • Manage the existing dropship catalogue on margin, cutting what doesn't pay.
  • First 90 days: paid spend cut on every SKU below 15% margin, even where that drops revenue. Google Ads moved in-house. First own-brand order placed. Attach offers live at checkout. Blended gross margin at 16%.

Requirements

Must have:

  • Launched a physical product end to end. Sourced it, negotiated MOQ, approved samples, managed freight, priced it, listed it, sold it
  • Run Google Ads yourself on a Shopping-led store. In the account, not briefing an agency
  • Owned a gross margin or P&L number, not a revenue or ROAS number
  • Operated at $500k-5m, where you wrote the product page and answered the customer emails
  • Comfortable cutting revenue to fix margin
  • Work independently. No team, no budget approver, nobody checking your work between weekly calls

Nice to have:

  • Built checkout attach, upsells or replenishment flows
  • Sold consumables or anything with repeat purchase
  • Worked with Chinese suppliers, or US co-packers and contract manufacturers
  • US import, duty classification, 3PL setup
  • Klaviyo or equivalent, built from scratch rather than inherited
  • Bundle and kit pricing
  • Preparedness, outdoor, hunting or adjacent category knowledge

We're also open to people from outside ecom. Founders whose company didn't work out, consultants who want to operate, anyone who has built something and can show it. The mechanics are learnable. The instinct isn't.

Not for you if you want a team, a budget, or someone telling you what to do next week. Or if a 25% revenue drop in month one would be a problem.

Benefits

€65-75,000 base. Equity from 5%, up to 10% earned against margin and profitability targets. Quarterly bonus on gross margin. Fully remote, anywhere in Europe, hours yours.

Small business, no funding behind it, everything pays for itself out of what the store makes. Take it through breakeven and to 25% margins with a real own-brand line and you own a meaningful piece of a profitable company you built.

Entropy sits inside a wider venture portfolio. If you get this working and want to build the next thing in this space, that conversation is open.

Send us your CV and tell us which brands you've worked on. Then one product you launched: what it was, what it cost landed, what it sold for, and what you got wrong. Two paragraphs.
